# FAQ page

Page type: FAQ

Frequently asked questions about Larkspur Supply Co. membership and rentals.

1. How much does membership cost? A lifetime membership costs $30, paid once.
2. What is the member dividend? Each spring, members get back a share of the profit, based on what they bought the year before. Last year it was 8%.
3. Can I rent gear without being a member? Yes. Members get 20% off rentals.
4. How do I return a rental? Bring it to the rental desk by closing time on the return date. Late returns cost one extra day.
5. Do you repair gear you didn't sell? Yes, we repair any brand. Estimates are free.
6. Can I cancel my membership? Yes. We refund your $30 if you cancel within 30 days.

Still have questions? Contact us (/contact).

Patterns combine semantic HTML with custom elements to create consistent, accessible structures. ## Philosophy Pages are composed of **blocks** - reusable content patterns that appear across many pages. By defining custom elements for these blocks, we: 1. **Communicate intent** - `` is clearer than `
` 2. **Enable styling** - Custom elements can be styled with CSS 3. **Support tooling** - Validators can enforce correct usage 4. **Document structure** - The markup is self-documenting ## Available Patterns | Pattern | Elements | Use Case | |---------|----------|----------| | [FAQ](#faq-pattern) | `faq-list`, `faq-question`, `faq-answer` | Q&A pages, help sections | | [Product Card](#product-card-pattern) | `product-card` | Product listings, catalogs | --- ## FAQ Pattern ### Elements ``` faq-list ├── faq-question ├── faq-answer ├── faq-question ├── faq-answer └── ... ``` ### Element Definitions | Element | Content | Attributes | |---------|---------|------------| | `faq-list` | `faq-question`, `faq-answer` | `category` (optional) | | `faq-question` | Phrasing content (text, links) | `id` (for anchor links) | | `faq-answer` | Flow content (paragraphs, lists) | - | ### Usage ```html

Products

What is your return policy? We offer a 30-day hassle-free return policy. How long does shipping take? Standard shipping takes 5-7 business days.
``` ### Complete FAQ Page Structure ```html

Frequently Asked Questions

  • Products
  • Shipping

Products

Question text? Answer text.

Still have questions?

Contact us

``` ### Accessibility Notes - Each section has `aria-labelledby` pointing to its heading - Questions have `id` attributes for direct linking - Table of contents uses `
` with descriptive `aria-label` - Links within answers use proper `mailto:` and `tel:` protocols --- ## Product Card Pattern ### Element Definition | Element | Content | Attributes | |---------|---------|------------| | `product-card` | Flow content | `sku`, `price` (optional) | ### Usage ```html

Widget Pro

Our best-selling widget with enhanced durability.

View details ``` ### Product Listing Structure ```html

Our Products

  • Basic Widget

    Entry-level widget for beginners.
``` --- ## Creating New Patterns When you identify a repeating content structure: 1. **Define the elements** in `elements.json` 2. **Document the pattern** in this skill 3. **Create an example** in the examples directory 4. **Add to project dictionary** if needed ### Element Naming Conventions - Use lowercase with hyphens: `pattern-element` - Be descriptive: `faq-question` not `fq` - Group related elements: `faq-list`, `faq-question`, `faq-answer` --- ## Page Type Patterns Beyond component blocks, entire page types follow patterns: | Page Type | Key Sections | |-----------|--------------| | Homepage | Hero, featured products, news, CTA | | About | History, mission, values, leadership, milestones | | Product List | Category nav, product grid, filters | | Product Detail | Hero, specs, reviews, related | | Contact | Info, form, map, hours | | FAQ | TOC nav, categorized Q&A sections | | Press Release | Headline, dateline, body, boilerplate, contacts | | Legal | Numbered sections, definitions, effective date | See individual examples in the `.claude/patterns/pages/` directory. ## Related Skills - **xhtml-author** - Write valid XHTML-strict HTML5 markup - **css-author** - Modern CSS organization with native @import, @layer casca... - **progressive-enhancement** - HTML-first development with CSS-only interactivity patterns - **forms** - HTML-first form patterns with CSS-only validation

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/htmlverify/eval/results/2026-10-18-pilot-abc/faq/B-1/work/.claude/skills/htmlverify # htmlverify htmlverify checks HTML as a browser parses it, against the WHATWG HTML standard, WAI-ARIA, the Vanilla Breeze vocabulary, and this project's house rules in `htmlverify.config.json`. A hook runs it after every write to an `.html` file, and its report comes back to you when the file fails. ## Workflow 1. Check: `npx htmlverify check page.html`. For a fragment, such as a component or a snippet, name the element it goes inside: `--context tbody`. 2. Apply the mechanical fixes: `npx htmlverify fix page.html --write`. They change only the form of the markup (quotes, case, `
`, boolean values, explicit tags, escaping, whitespace), never the parsed tree. 3. Fix the rest by hand, errors first. `npx htmlverify explain ` says why a rule exists and shows a failing and a passing example. 4. Check again. Stop after three rounds, or when the same finding survives two rounds, and report what remains. 5. Hand back the result with its status and its open review items. ## Reading a report - `error` fails the file; `warning` and `info` don't. - Each finding gives its rule, its position, and what to do. `[fix]` marks one that `fix` applies. - `review` lines are questions only a person can answer, such as whether an alt text describes its image. Pass them on to the user; never answer them yourself. - `untested` lists checks that didn't run. Don't claim they passed. ## Rules of engagement - Fix the cause, not the rule. Never turn rules off, lower their severity, or edit `htmlverify.config.json` to get a pass. - Never invent content to satisfy a check: no made-up alt text, labels, captions, titles, or review answers. Ask the user for the real content. - Use Vanilla Breeze elements and attributes as declared; the messages name the declared ones. Don't rename an element to an ad-hoc `x-*` one to get past `component/unknown-element`. - Prefer native HTML to ARIA on generic elements: `
